title: Beyond the 956: Marcos Camino, founder of Los Palmeras, dies at 76
excerpt: Marcos Camino, the founding accordionist and musical leader of the legendary Argentine cumbia group Los Palmeras, has died at 76. He died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Santa Fe, Argentina, the group confirmed in an official statement.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Marcos Camino, the founding accordionist and musical leader of the legendary Argentine cumbia group Los Palmeras, has died at 76.

Camino died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Santa Fe, Argentina. He was found in the band's recording studio in the Candioti Norte neighborhood of Santa Fe. Los Palmeras confirmed his death in an official statement and asked for respect for the family's privacy. Authorities are investigating the circumstances.

Camino was born Marcos Máximo Camino on August 31, 1950, in Santa Fe. He co-founded Los Palmeras on December 9, 1972, and spent more than five decades as the group's accordionist, musical director, and driving force, shaping the sound of cumbia santafesina and carrying it to audiences across Argentina and Latin America.

With Los Palmeras, Camino helped build one of the most beloved catalogs in tropical music, including hits such as "El bombón asesino," "La cola," "Olvidala," and "Soy sabalero," the anthem embraced by fans of Colón de Santa Fe. The group became a fixture at festivals and dance halls across the region, and its songs remain staples of cumbia playlists throughout Latin America.

In February 2026, Camino announced his retirement from the stage, citing his age and health, after more than 50 years with the band he helped create. His death comes months after the group said goodbye to its longtime singer, Rubén "Cacho" Deícas, who left the group in 2025.

Rest in Peace, Marcos Camino.

Sources: Los Palmeras (official statement, November 10, 2026); El Trece TV; Ciudad Magazine; Radio Mitre; El Tribuno.
